decisions.note: At 700 dpi the colon of «[الناس:» sits as close to the 6 as the digits sit to each other, so no word space is printed. «](ثلاثًا)» is set closed up, with ] touching (. This matches b17 d022 for the same layout on p.068. European digits are kept, in logical order 1-6.
At 700 dpi «[الفاتحة:١-٧]» is printed tight, with the colon touching ١. Compare «[الصافات: ١٨٠-١٨٢]» on the same page, which has a clear space.

At 1200 dpi a kasra is printed low under the final ha of the Allah ligature, separate from the kasra under the ba. The Name has a printed case vowel, so it is written with all its marks per CONVENTIONS §2 (اللَّهُ/ٱللَّهِ example), as in b17/b21/b27: بِاللَّهِ.
At 800 dpi «[طه:١١١]» is printed tight after the colon, while «[آل عمران: ١-٢]» on the line above has a clear space.

At 800 dpi nothing is printed over ٱللَّهِ before the closing bracket of 16:53, and the quotation ends there. Genuine print variant. Waqf signs of this size, e.g. ۖ over وَٰحِدٌ on p.071, are clearly visible elsewhere.
At 700 dpi the short 2:255 quotation on p.071 ends «ٱلْقَيُّومُ﴾» with no ۚ printed. Genuine print variant at the end of the quoted span.
At 700 dpi nothing is printed over ٱلْقَيُّومِ before the closing bracket of 20:111, and the quotation ends there. Genuine print variant.

print_errors.note: The preposition is printed «إلي» with two dots under the final letter, not «إلى» (checked at 1600 dpi; no small alif either). Kept as printed. On the same page «إلى ﴿وَمَا بِكُم…» is printed correctly with alef maqsura.
The footnote ends without a final period. Nothing was added.

keyA.notes: Markers: p.068 ends with a complete sentence («…[الفلق:1-5](ثَلاثًا).»), there are no footnotes on p.068, and p.069 starts with a new basmala + al-Nas, so p.069 has no '+'. p.070 continues the sentence «…بعض آيات الذكر / الحكيم، ثُمَّ…» from p.069, so it is <<<ص:070+>>>. p.071 starts with the heading, so no '+'. p.072 continues Ayat al-Kursi (2:255) from the end of p.071 («…يَعْلَمُ / مَا بَيْنَ…»), so it is <<<ص:072+>>>. Because validate.py needs balanced brackets on each line, the 2:255 quotation is closed with ﴾ after «يَعْلَمُ» at the end of p.071 and reopened with ﴿ before «مَا بَيْنَ» at the start of p.072. Neither bracket is printed at the page break (same handling as p.066/067 in b17). Fatiha on p.069: the print opens the ornate bracket before the basmala and gives it ayah number (١), so it is written inside the brackets as ayah 1: ﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ (١) ٱلْحَمْدُ…﴾. The other surah basmalas (al-Nas, al-Asr, Al Imran, Ghafir, 2:163 block) are printed before the bracket and are written outside it. References: European digits on p.069 «[الناس:1-6]». The print shows 6 next to the colon and 1 on the left, the same bidi layout as p.068, so the logical order is 1-6. Spacing after the colon was measured at 900 dpi: about 40-49 px (about 3-4 pt, no more than the gaps between digits) for الناس / الفاتحة / طه, so no space is written ([الناس:1-6], [الفاتحة:١-٧], [طه:١١١]); about 78-79 px for الصافات / العصر, so a space is written. The other references (النحل, البقرة, آل عمران, غافر) clearly have a space. «](ثلاثًا)» on p.069: the gap is 27 px, smaller than the digit gaps, so no space is written (as on p.068). This «ثلاثًا» has fathatan only. «[الفاتحة:١-٧]. آمين» keeps the printed period, and «آمين» is plain. A space is always written between ﴾ and [. Quran encoding follows CONVENTIONS §3 / Tanzil: the round silent zero ۟ on ءَامَنُوا۟، وَعَمِلُوا۟، وَتَوَاصَوْا۟، تُبْدُوا۟، وَقَالُوا۟ (checked at up to 2000 dpi; it is distinct from the khāʾ-head sukun on the waw of وَتَوَاصَوْا۟); the iqlab mim on ٱلذَّنۢبِ; the small waw/yeh with madda on عِندَهُۥٓ and عِلْمِهِۦٓ; فِىٓ (2:284) with madda; الٓمٓ and حمٓ with madda; the kashida hamza seat يَـُٔودُهُۥ and the ئِ of وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتِهِۦ in the Tanzil form. Waqf signs are written where printed. scripts/quran.py reports only 3 waqf signs that Tanzil has at the end of a quoted span: 16:53 ٱللَّهِ ۖ, 2:255 ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ (the short quotation on p.071) and 20:111 ٱلْقَيُّومِ ۖ. I checked the image at each one: none is printed, and none was added. The rub el-hizb ۞ that Tanzil puts before 20:111 is not printed either. Body text: «تُقْرأ» (p.069) has damma on the ta and a sukun on the qaf (the two marks are stacked; checked at 2400 dpi), and the hamza on the alif carries no vowel. «جُلُوسًا» has dammas on both jim and lam. Final ى in the body font (حتى، إلى) is written plain. On p.071 the isti'adha line «أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ…» has a printed kasra under the ha of the Allah ligature (checked at 1000-1800 dpi; it sits low, under the ha, separate from the kasras of السَّمِيعِ). Following CONVENTIONS §2 and b17 practice (case vowel printed → write all marks), it is written بِاللَّهِ. «(الله)» on p.069 and «إلى الله التجا» on p.071 have no case vowel, so they are plain الله. «اللَّهُمَّ» on p.070 is explicitly vowelled. «إِلَهَ» in the p.070 dua has no dagger alif (checked at 2000 dpi). p.071: the title is the # heading «الوظيفة الزروقيَّة» (shadda+fatha on the yeh, as printed; the print sets الوظيفةالزروقيَّة nearly touching). The four lines under it are plain paragraphs. «المسماة بـ (سفينة…)» has a tatweel after the ba. CONVENTIONS §2 drops tatweel and validate.py rejects it, so it is written «المسماة ب (سفينة النجا لمن إلى الله التجا)»; an adjudicator may want to check this. The note line «وتقرأ في جماعة يوميا…» is in a smaller font, plain, with no tanween on يوميا. Nothing on these pages is bold in contrast to its surroundings: the Quran on pp.071-072 is set in a heavier mushaf face and the dua on p.070 in the vowelled font, and neither is bold markup. The digits ٣٣ and (٢٠) are in the regular digit face. On p.069 «نحو (٢٠) مرة» has a space before the parenthesis, so it is not a footnote. The only footnote is p.070 (١), glued to «ودنياهم(١).». In the footnote «بالمقطم.وينصح» and «الحضرةجماعيًا» are set tight, and word spaces are written. Running heads (p.071 still prints «المعارف الذوقية في الوظيفة الصديقية»; p.072 prints «الوظيفة الزروقية»), page numbers, bracket flowers and ayah-number ornaments are omitted, except for the digits inside them.

print_errors.note: The preposition is printed with a dotted final ي (إلي) here, while إلى elsewhere on the page has no dots. Kept as printed.

keyB.notes: p069: p068 ends with a complete sentence «(ثلاثًا).» and has no footnotes, so the marker has no + and there is no (تابع). The An-Nas reference uses European digits: it looks like «6-1» in print and is written in reading order as [الناس: 1-6], the same way as the p068 example in CONVENTIONS. The space between ] and «(ثلاثًا)» matches keyB b17 (in print the ] touches the parenthesis). In the Fatiha, the basmala is printed in full size inside ﴿ as ayah (١), so it is written inside the brackets. The ﴾ and [ of the Saffat reference touch in print and the colons in «[الفاتحة:١-٧]» and «[طه:١١١]» are set tight; all three are written with the usual spacing «﴾ [سورة: n]». The bold-looking digits ٣٣ and (٢٠) are the normal heavy Arabic-Indic digits of the body font, not bold markup. p070: continues p069 («آيات الذكر / الحكيم») so it is marked +; footnote (١) has no final period in print. p071: the heading is printed as «الوظيفةالزروقيَّة» with no visible space; it is written per the STRUCTURE heading map. «المسماة بـ (سفينة …)» is printed with a tatweel after ب; the tatweel is dropped per §2, which leaves «ب (سفينة». In «أَعُوذُ بِاللهِ» only the printed kasra is written on the Allah ligature, as in keyB b14. Ayat al-Kursi runs from p071 onto p072 within one paragraph (p072 marked +). The print has no bracket at the page break, but validate.py needs ﴿﴾ balanced on each line, so ﴾ was added after «يَعْلَمُ» at the end of p071 and ﴿ before «مَا بَيْنَ» at the start of p072. A merge should remove these two brackets when the pages are joined. Waqf signs that Tanzil has at the end of the quoted fragments (16:53 ۖ, 2:255 ۚ after ٱلْقَيُّومُ on p071, 20:111 ۖ) are not printed and were not added. Every Quran span was checked word by word against the zoomed print. scripts/quran.py reports no other differences from Tanzil.
